deviations_from_card: Case 4: the card's literal CSS (--bd-ink-3: var(--bd-ink-2) and --bd-ink-4: var(--bd-ink-3) on the same element) resolves ink-4 to ink-2, because var() resolves on the same element - three rungs collapse into one. Built instead: root scope re-points ink-4 -> its unmoved ink-3 and rule -> rule-2; the wrapper re-points ink-3 -> ink-2 and rule -> rule-2 and takes ink-4 by `inherit` from root, so inside the board the ladder is ink, ink-2, ink-2, ink-3 as the card intends. Root keeps its own ink-3 (already 7.81:1; nothing at root scope sets a quiet rung). The test resolves both scopes with same-element var() semantics and was confirmed to go red on the card's literal version. Also beyond the card's six marks: rest carousel dots become ButtonText rings (they were fill-only, border 0, and vanished), the score axis gets a CanvasText outline, the fire button's hover and disabled states are answered (the coral hover rule outranks the base one and would survive forced-color-adjust: none), and the two focusable opt-outs name outline-color: CanvasText. The hover override sets only background/border-color to satisfy hover.test.ts's transition rule.
